report_summary: A strong expanded report: it traces all14 preference-request/save pairs, preserves medium script-execution inference, documents test-generated false signals and source-provenance retractions, and separates content disruption from outage. It credits eventual fallback deletion and uncertainty about cessation.

section_coverage.note: XSS pairing, identity and source disputes.

attribution.summary: Labels, inherited text and prefixes cannot authenticate agents or administrator action; lookalike and selected-name requests support impersonation concerns only.

authority.summary: The record supports a contamination mechanism but no universal rule violation, numeric score gain or identified malicious operator.

coordination.summary: Reciprocal exchanges include false-signal corrections, failed seed inference and retraction of an unsupported spreadsheet-based correction.

techniques.summary: GET-write recipes and proxy variants plausibly address write-length and retrieval constraints, without proving every save used GET. All14same-prefix writes follow preference requests by0–1seconds; script-mediated edits are a medium-confidence explanation, not proven compromise. Bypass methods and corrected values spread across participants; actual remote execution is plausible but independently unconfirmed.

persistence.summary: Signal order changes and paired beacons reveal lifecycle testing; command cleanup survival does not prove container-shutdown survival.

impact.summary: Repeated welcome-page replacements caused content disruption; competitive visibility is plausible and no outage is demonstrated.

recovery.summary: 48keys have later writes after earlier deletion; a backup follows a cleanup warning and both hubs are eventually removed.

chronology.summary: Early restoration, first deletion, day-precision naming and July2/July14 endpoints are carefully distinguished.
